commitResults.messageBody: Move command input, greetings, dividers, errors, task displays, and confirmation messages out of Chai. This gives the main application one UI dependency and separates presentation concerns without changing CLI behavior.

Move application classes under the chai package and group task, storage, and UI classes into focused subpackages. Add read-only task accessors so persistence respects package boundaries while keeping src/main/java as the source root.

commitResults.messageTitle: Configure Gradle to build and run Chai
commitResults.messageBody: Point the application plugin at the packaged chai.Chai entry point and name the executable shadow JAR chai.jar after merging the provided Gradle wrapper support.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for commands and dated tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Test command keyword classification across known, mixed-case, empty, and unknown inputs. Test deadline and event rendering across date boundaries and completion-state transitions using JUnit 5 through Gradle.
Chai and its main method are public APIs but have no header comments. Add concise Javadocs that explain the class responsibility and command-line entry point.

Several public APIs have summaries but omit parameter and return contracts, which causes the Javadoc task to report warnings. Document those contracts and enum values so generated API documentation is complete and warning-free.

Future Java changes need a concise, repository-local summary of the required coding standard. Add a reusable skill that points to the authoritative guide and captures the rules that affect implementation and review decisions.

Commit and tagging work needs a reusable summary of the project's Git conventions. Add a focused skill covering atomic changes, imperative subjects, explanatory bodies, and safe handling of generated files and tags.

The repository now contains reusable Java and Git standard skills, but agents need an explicit instruction to apply them. Route future Java and commit work through those skills from the project-level agent guidance.

Chai's switch cases are aligned with the switch rather than indented within it, and one trailing comment records tool provenance instead of explaining intent. Reformat the switch and remove incidental comments so the source follows the mandated layout and comment rules.
Users cannot locate tasks without reading the entire list. Add a find command that matches keywords against task descriptions without regard to letter case and displays only the matching tasks.

Find relies on task descriptions matching exact, partial, and differently cased keywords while rejecting absent terms. Cover those cases directly so regressions in search behavior are detected independently of console output.

Add SE-EDU-aligned style rules and enable Checkstyle 14.1.0 for main and test sources. Fix existing import-order and switch-indentation violations so the checks provide a clean baseline.

commitResults.messageTitle: Decouple command responses from console UI
commitResults.messageBody: Expose Chai responses through a reusable session API so the existing console and the upcoming JavaFX interface can share the same command logic.

Launch Chai through a responsive FXML-based conversation window with reusable dialog controls and CSS styling. Package cross-platform JavaFX dependencies and retain the console-backed command engine for testability.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use varargs for console message batches
commitResults.messageBody: Allow the console UI to print any number of ordered messages through one helper, reducing repetitive output calls while keeping the interaction format unchanged.

Add assertions at task construction boundaries to make assumptions about descriptions and dates explicit. These checks expose programming errors during development without replacing validation for user input.

Move syntax validation and value conversion into a dedicated Parser so Chai can focus on coordinating task operations. Direct parser tests now cover valid and malformed commands without involving storage or UI code.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a stream to filter matching tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Express keyword search as a filter operation over the task collection. The stream preserves task order and removes temporary mutation while keeping the resulting list local to response formatting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Define chronological ordering dates for tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Expose a consistent date key for mixed task types so sorting logic does not need type checks. Todos use a final sentinel date, which keeps them after dated tasks while preserving stable insertion order.
Let users persistently reorder deadlines by due date and events by start date while keeping todos afterward. Reject sort arguments to keep the command predictable and document the new behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle malformed commands and saved data
commitResults.messageBody:
Accept harmless command casing and spacing variations while rejecting
unexpected arguments. Validate stored descriptions and console EOF so bad
input cannot terminate Chai with an internal exception.

Improve command, storage, and console error handling while preserving
valid command behavior.

Inject the data-file path so persistence tests use isolated temporary
directories. Cover successful round trips and environmental or malformed
data failures, including escaped storage delimiters in descriptions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give Chai a calm tea-house personality
commitResults.messageBody:
Align the welcome, confirmations, errors, title, avatar, prompt, and
colors around a warm task-brewing theme. Keep responses concise so the
personality supports rather than obscures task management.

application.
